objective: Under G18, at the coordinator's pick (the advisor's direction 3): write one statement, with stated hypotheses and a stated definition of a free sender, that for laws reading no values puts every recorded table above CHSH 2 (or a Mermin-type bound) in one of three kinds: (a) separate responses in which each setting birth multiplies an old word's weight by a factor set by its own setting and the old state (a local model with partial rejection); (b) a response depending on both settings (a shared birth or a whole-round event), which signals once a sender may condition on what it sees; (c) a supplied order, sign or reading. Class every row of the record (the two-countings table, 9/4, 7/3, 5/2, 104/45, 61/30, the third-holder family, the sign and side-sign readings). Stop when all rows are classed, or at a row that fits none; say where the hypotheses exclude patterns with allowed parts and no allowed whole.
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (obstruction learned, with one opening; an argument with a classification; referee pending): under one state of the whole every recorded table above the classical bound is separate responses reweighted by the counting, a response or record depending on both settings, or something supplied; none fits none. Theorem K: a free sender always exposes an excess of separate responses; but a free sender keys a birth to a value, which no law does, so inside the model some excesses stay hidden.
title: Three kinds: one statement that classes every recorded table above the classical bound
